title: Neuropsychological Case Profile: Phineas Gage & Patient H.M.
description: Analyze classic clinical cases linking localized brain damage to specific cognitive and behavioral deficits.
problemStatement:
Examine the two most famous lesion cases in neurobiology: Phineas Gage (1848) and Patient H.M. (1953).

### Requirements:
1. For Phineas Gage: Describe the exact anatomical lesion (orbitofrontal cortex) and contrast his pre-accident personality with his post-accident behavioral dysregulation.
2. For Patient H.M.: Detail the bilateral resection of the medial temporal lobe/hippocampus and explain the difference between anterograde amnesia for explicit facts versus preserved procedural motor skills.
3. Formulate a conclusion on how focal lesion studies propelled localization of function in neuropsychology.
hints: Hint 1: Gage retained intelligence and memory, but lost emotional impulse inhibition.
Hint 2: H.M. could learn the mirror-tracing task despite having no conscious memory of having practiced it.
